sections.E: The existing MU, AMD, ANET and NVDA holdings constitute the shared AI-infrastructure exposure described in the supplied portfolio and research narratives. Treat that classification as a risk framework, not measured independent diversification. Hypothetical common shock: customers delay infrastructure purchases while financing becomes more expensive. MU could face pricing pressure alongside capital spending; AMD could carry supply commitments without matching profitable sales; ANET could suffer concentrated-customer spending reductions; NVDA could experience slower collections and margin pressure. Earnings disappointment and multiple contraction could coincide. [MU | net_debt: -33185000000 USD | as-of 2026-09-03 | FMP/balance-sheet-statement | snapshot 2f62c44f6fbb], [AMD | net_debt: -810000000 USD | as-of 2026-06-27 | FMP/balance-sheet-statement | snapshot 2f62c44f6fbb] and [ANET | total_debt: 0 USD | as-of 2026-06-30 | FMP/balance-sheet-statement | snapshot 2f62c44f6fbb] support issuer financing resilience, not protection against equity losses; [NVDA | net_debt: 16417000000 USD | as-of 2026-07-26 | FMP/balance-sheet-statement | snapshot 2f62c44f6fbb] indicates a different financing position. Retaining existing sizing is a discretionary acceptance of substantial correlated downside because dated profitability and positive free cash flow still support ownership. It is not justified by the return ambition or recent gains, and exposure is not increased while valuation and cash-quality questions remain unresolved. Verified common demand deterioration warrants joint review rather than waiting for every quarterly monitor to fail. Cash is buying power, not a protective cushion. Preferred potential deployment is MU after supported normalized earnings and contract economics, or AMD/ANET after evidence of profitable incremental demand at an attractive refreshed valuation. These are research criteria, not promised purchases. No calibrated probability supports Kelly-optimal sizing.
